terms.def: A KMSC staff member who works at a site. Each operator is responsible for a set of phones. There is one operator for every ten phones. The operator hands out the phones, restarts them, and manages the wearers.
The person who wears the phone and records the video. A wearer is an employee of the site, or a worker we recruited. Every wearer passes onboarding screening.
The set of sites that one Portfolio Manager owns. Each portfolio has a monthly hour target.

The setup day at a new site. It happens before official filming starts. On launch day we set up the stations, put on the labels, set up the network, give the orientation, and make the pilot recordings.
One recording period of 30 minutes. The collection app stops recording after 30 minutes. Then the phone is restarted, and the next cycle starts.
The report that the Portfolio Manager sends to Mano at the end of the day. It lists the hours, the active phones, the hardware, the problems, and the fixes.

A note about one video, written during review. There are two kinds of flag. A feedback flag means there is something to fix. A fraud flag means the video is not paid, there is a penalty, and there is a risk of a ban.
A warning on an account. After two strikes, the phone is paused. The phone stays paused until the worker is retrained.
The unique ID of one recorded video in the export. QC uses the session ID to link a flag to one specific video.
The record that shows who wore which phone on which shift.
Footage that was recorded but is not uploaded yet. We measure backlog in device-days. If a site has more than one day of backlog, that is an incident.
A place with a fast internet line. We bring the phones to the depot, and they upload overnight.
The checklist that every wearer completes before a phone goes on their head.
The daily meeting of Adham, Moharam, and Mano.
Thirty minutes every day. In this time, any operator can talk directly to leadership.
A performance improvement plan that lasts 7 days. It comes with a written warning.
If you bring us a site contract, you get 10% on that contract. If you refer a person and we hire them, you get 2,000 EGP.
Any place where people expect more privacy than usual. We never film there.

ownership: Mano owns this map. He approves every change. Every edit gets one line in the changelog, with a version and a date.

changelog.text: We rebuilt the map as a site. Every section is now its own page. We moved the content into JSON files. We added channels, incident playbooks, training, metrics, risks, the never list, the letter generator, the capacity calculator, six more manual subsystems, Arabic for the pages that workers use, and print styles.

The whole map was on one page. It had the people, who to call, the workflow with nine stages, the working day, the rules, onboarding screening, the glossary, and the first two manual subsystems. Those two were data logistics and asset control.
